facts: LlamaForCausalLM HF4.31 shifts labels/logits, flattens all batch tokens, and calls default torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss().

torch2.6 default reduction is mean and ignore_index is -100. For integer labels with no class weight, each microbatch scalar is sum CE over nonignored shifted targets divided by their count. Padding/input masks reduce this count; input length alone is not the denominator.
Trainer4.31 passes raw model loss to accelerator.backward. Its detached return division by accumulation is for training-loss accounting and does not apply an additional backward scaling.

Accelerate0.21 skips its usual loss/gradient_accumulation division under DeepSpeed and delegates to engine.backward then engine.step. DS0.16.9 scales backward loss by GAS once; ZeRO reduce-scatter averages across DP ranks. The BF16 loss scaler factor is1.0. None of these components aggregates a global unmasked-token denominator across distinct microbatches.

derivation.notation: n_i=number of nonignored labels AFTER causal shift; s_i=sum of their CE losses; t_i=s_i/n_i. Assume nonzero n_i and identical examples/forward semantics, before clipping/Adam and floating-point effects.
derivation.general: L_(W,A,m)=(1/(W*A))*sum_(rank r, accumulation a)[ (sum_(i in microbatch B_ra) s_i)/(sum_(i in B_ra) n_i) ].
derivation.official_layout: W8,A2,m8 gives average of16 separate eight-example token means. It is not generally a single global128-example token mean.
derivation.candidate_layout: W2,A64,m1 gives (1/128)*sum_i t_i, i.e. equal-example mean of each individual answer token mean.
derivation.inequality: With varying n_i, coefficients of each example/token generally change even when128 examples and their order are fixed. This can change task weights when response lengths differ; it is not limited to floating-point roundoff.
derivation.special_case: When every example in the compared effective batch has the same n_i, the reduction-weight difference vanishes algebraically. Other numerical/order/topology/initialization differences remain.
